html:
Kazembe is a kingdom in the Luapula valley near Lake Mweru, on today's border of Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, founded by a Lunda general in the 1700s. The map shows it in its 1815 snapshot, near the height of its power.

Its kings, each called Mwata Kazembe, first ruled as a western outpost of the Lunda empire and then on their own. The kingdom sat on rich fishing grounds and on trade routes that ran to both coasts. It sent copper, ivory and slaves west to Angola and east toward Mozambique, and Portuguese expeditions came to its capital in 1798 and 1831. David Livingstone visited later.

From the 1850s the trader Msiri built the Yeke kingdom on its western side and took much of its trade. In the 1890s British forces from Northern Rhodesia brought it under colonial rule. The kingship survives, with its yearly Mutomboko ceremony.
